title: Behavior contract
description: One business rule, the workflows it applies to, the evidence for it, and executable scenarios that verify can run against any implementation. Written by `contract`, approved by a person, executed by `verify`.

version.description: Bumped whenever the rule, parameters or scenarios change.

statement.description: The rule in one plain-English sentence a business owner would sign off.

status.description: Only approved contracts are enforced by verify.

workflows.description: Every workflow this rule must hold on. The rare ones matter most.

operation.description: Business operation, e.g. 'POST /api/order'. Bindings map this onto each implementation.

observed.description: How many times the watcher saw it.

expression.description: The rule as a formula over outcome fields.

parameters.description: Per-entity values the rule depends on, e.g. each account's rate.

scenarios.description: Executable checks. verify runs each through a binding for the old app and the new app and compares the outcome with `expect`.

input.description: Business inputs, in canonical units (money in integer cents).

expect.description: Expected business outcome, in canonical units. Plain keys are outcome fields compared exactly. For an operation that returns several records, list them in `records` (matched by partId); `count` and `totalCents` check the set as a whole.

repeat.description: Optional retry check, e.g. { times: 2, idempotencyKey: 'k1', expectRecords: 1 }.

evidence.description: Where the rule came from. Every claim in the contract should trace to at least one item.

source.description: Table, log file, code path or .reel folder.

refs.description: Row ids, line numbers or timestamps (seconds).

provenance.description: What we know and how. Keeps observed facts apart from guesses and from human decisions.
